 Politiko Lokal Fake Filipinos beware: NBI probes networks behind citizenship fraud
 NBI Director Melvin Matibag orders a nationwide probe into fraudulently procured Philippine citizenship documents to protect national security.
 By King Kenneth Gaborne October 22, 2026 3:33 PM National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag has ordered a nationwide investigation of fraudulently procured Philippine citizenship documents.
 “This is about protecting the integrity of the Republic’s institutions,” said Matibag on Thursday (Oct. 22).
 “Philippine citizenship carries constitutional rights, privileges and responsibilities,” the NBI chief pointed out.
 Because of this, he stressed that the government must ensure that the documents used to establish identity and citizenship have not been manufactured, falsified or fraudulently obtained to penetrate institutions, conceal criminal activity, acquire property unlawfully, or circumvent restrictions imposed by the Constitution and Philippine laws.
 Matibag has already issued a memorandum dated Oct. 20 and addressed to the NBI’s regional directors who were ordered to conduct the investigation.
 “The objective is not simply to discover a fake document,” said the director.
 “We want to determine who produced it, who facilitated it, who benefited from it, what institutions were compromised, what assets were acquired through it, and whether an organized criminal or national-security network exists behind it,” he added.
 In his memorandum, Matibag told regional directors to submit an initial inventory of validated subjects, suspected networks, facilitators, investigative status and identified assets within 90 days.
 If there are cases with immediate national-security implications, active transnational-crime threats, imminent dissipation of assets or ongoing corruption to be reported immediately, he told the directors to immediately issue a report.
